name: Intuit Inc.

profile.description: Intuit is a global financial technology platform behind TurboTax, QuickBooks, Credit Karma, and Mailchimp, serving consumers, small businesses, and accountants with tax, accounting, credit, and marketing tools. FY2026 (ended July 31, 2026) revenue rose 14% to $21.45B with GAAP diluted EPS of $16.46. In May 2026, CEO Sasan Goodarzi cut about 17% of the workforce (~3,000 roles) to simplify the organization, and Intuit signed multi-year agreements to embed Anthropic and OpenAI models in its products and make its tools available inside Claude and ChatGPT.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Innovation Track Record (3/3): Intuit has transformed from desktop tax software to cloud SaaS and then into a multi-product platform through Credit Karma and Mailchimp, growing revenue from $9.63B in FY2021 to $21.45B in FY2026 [1][3]. AI Deployment (2/2): AI-driven 'Big Bets' were credited with accelerating growth in the FY2026 Q4 report ($4.35B revenue vs. $4.27B consensus), and new multi-year agreements embed Anthropic and OpenAI models in Intuit products while distributing Intuit tools inside Claude and ChatGPT [1][4][5]. Market Share Leadership (2/2): TurboTax and QuickBooks are the category-defining consumer tax and small-business accounting platforms in the U.S. [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): FY2027 guidance of $23.28-$23.51B revenue (9-10% growth) and Q1 guidance of $4.29-$4.31B (+11%) give visibility, but no dated next-generation product launches with revenue targets were disclosed [4]. R&D Intensity (1/1): FY2026 R&D of $3.38B equals 15.7% of revenue, top-tier for application software [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): 'Powering prosperity around the world' is a specific mission that frames financial software as economic empowerment for consumers and small businesses, and it has guided acquisitions such as Credit Karma [1]. Community Impact (1/2): Intuit publishes stakeholder impact reporting and carries a low Sustainalytics ESG risk score (13.29) and an MSCI AAA rating, but no distinctive dollar-quantified community program was found in this review [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Intuit cut about 17% of its global workforce (~3,000 roles) in May 2026 with ~$340M of restructuring charges [6]. Insider Buying (1/2): Director Vasant Prabhu bought 1,750 shares at ~$309-$310 (~$540K) in May 2026, the only open-market purchases in years; the CEO and other executives did not buy [8].

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock (weighted 9.92/10). D/E of 44.3%, ROE of 23.6% (2x), profit margin of 21.3%, revenue growth of 13.7% YoY, and forward P/E of 12.7 all meet or beat their targets and score 1.0 [2]. The 5-year revenue CAGR of 17.4% (FMP, $9.63B in FY2021 to $21.45B in FY2026) scores 1.0 at 2x weight [3]. The only metric short of target is the Yahoo-reported PEG of 1.08, scoring 0.96 at 2x weight [2]. The stock has halved from its 52-week high of $682 to $341, compressing valuation. Liquidity floor cleared: 3.63M shares x $341.09 = ~$1.24B daily.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): AI is a real substitution threat — the stock is down ~50% from its 52-week high amid fears that LLM-based tools commoditize tax prep and small-business bookkeeping, FY2027 TurboTax growth is guided to only 2-3%, and lower average revenue per TurboTax customer and Mailchimp weakness were cited in the guidance miss [2][4]. Goodarzi argues stand-alone LLMs lack the validation guardrails needed for high-stakes tax and accounting, and Intuit's proprietary financial data, regulatory integrations, and accountant network give it defensible moats [6]. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI-driven 'Big Bets' were credited with accelerating FY2026 Q4 growth, and the Anthropic and OpenAI distribution agreements monetize Intuit's tools inside third-party AI assistants [5][6].

infinite_game.summary: Intuit has a genuine, long-lived purpose and a CEO willing to make costly bets — reinventing products around AI and partnering with the very AI labs that threaten it. Sinek would applaud that courage and the decision to treat AI labs as partners rather than enemies, but would see the 17% layoff of May 2026 as a breach of the Circle of Safety that undermines the trust an infinite organization depends on.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Powering prosperity around the world' has persisted across CEO transitions from Scott Cook to Brad Smith to Sasan Goodarzi and shapes strategy, including the Credit Karma acquisition and the focus on consumers and small businesses [1]. It is genuine and partially lived, but the 2026 layoffs and margin-driven restructuring show the cause has not consistently won out over efficiency.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Intuit eliminated about 3,000 roles (17% of staff) in May 2026, targeting 'coordination-heavy' roles such as project managers and business operations staff, with ~$340M of severance-heavy restructuring charges [6]. Goodarzi framed the cuts as removing management layers that slowed innovation, but a cut of this scale signals to remaining employees that their safety is conditional — the opposite of Sinek's Circle of Safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Rather than fighting AI labs, Intuit signed multi-year agreements to embed Anthropic and OpenAI models in its products and to make its tax, accounting, and marketing tools available inside Claude and ChatGPT [6]. Treating the companies whose technology most threatens its franchise as partners and sources of capability is a textbook infinite response to competition.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Intuit has evolved from boxed desktop software to cloud subscriptions to an AI-driven platform, and expanded into credit and marketing via Credit Karma and Mailchimp [1][3]. Each step has been an evolution of the same tax-and-accounting franchise rather than abandoning a core business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): Goodarzi has repeatedly accepted near-term pain for long-term positioning — guiding FY2027 growth down to 9-10% (shares fell ~12% on the guide), switching non-GAAP reporting to include share-based compensation (cutting reported EPS guidance to $22.88-$23.12 from $24.27 in FY2026), and opening Intuit's tools to rival AI platforms [4][5][6]. Combined with sustained R&D of 15.7% of revenue during a 50% share-price drawdown, this is a pattern of choosing capability and transparency over flattering near-term numbers [2][3].

investment_thesis: Intuit combines elite financials with a valuation reset. FY2026 revenue grew 14% to $21.45B, GAAP diluted EPS rose 20% to $16.46, and the five-year revenue CAGR is 17.4%, with a 21% net margin, 23.6% ROE, and only 44% D/E [1][2][3]. After falling from $682 to $341, the stock trades at 12.7x forward earnings with a 1.08 PEG, while FY2027 guidance still calls for 9-10% revenue growth and Q1 revenue growth of 11% [2][4]. The Anthropic and OpenAI agreements position Intuit's tax and accounting engines as the trusted back end for AI assistants rather than a casualty of them [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that AI erodes the franchise faster than Intuit can adapt. FY2027 TurboTax growth is guided to only 2-3%, average revenue per TurboTax customer is falling, Mailchimp is weak, and desktop products are declining [4]. The 17% workforce reduction and ~$340M restructuring charge raise execution and morale risk, a 2026 securities class action is pending, and the switch to including stock compensation in non-GAAP EPS makes guidance look lower ($22.88-$23.12 vs. $24.27 in FY2026) [5][6][7].
key_catalysts: Q1 FY2027 results — guidance of $4.29-$4.31B revenue (+11%) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.44-$2.48; beating it would ease fears of an AI-driven slowdown [4]
Monetization of AI distribution — Anthropic and OpenAI agreements put Intuit's tax, accounting, and marketing tools inside Claude and ChatGPT, opening new customer acquisition channels [6]
Margin expansion from restructuring — the May 2026 removal of ~3,000 coordination-heavy roles should lower operating costs from FY2027 onward [6]
key_risks: AI commoditization of tax and bookkeeping — TurboTax growth guided to just 2-3% for FY2027 with declining revenue per customer [4]
Organizational disruption — a 17% workforce cut (~3,000 roles) could hurt morale and execution during a critical product transition [6]
Mailchimp and desktop decline — weaker Mailchimp revenue and declining desktop products were key drivers of the FY2027 guidance miss [4]
